claims.claim: Marvell is positioned across two AI-infrastructure bottlenecks: custom compute silicon and high-speed connectivity/electro-optics. Q2 FY2027 data-center revenue was $2.172B, 79% of company revenue, with 46% year-over-year growth.

The causal chain is AI cluster scale -> specialized compute plus interconnect demand -> hyperscaler custom designs/connectivity silicon -> Marvell production revenue; the principal successor bottlenecks are advanced foundry, packaging, substrate and outsourced test capacity.

Structural resilience is mixed: custom silicon deepens customer integration and optical interconnect broadens exposure, but hyperscaler vertical integration can simultaneously create Marvell design opportunities and substitute Marvell out of other sockets.

claims.claim: Current growth is real but increasingly concentrated: data center represented 79% of Q2 FY2027 revenue, and Marvell itself flags dependence on a few customers and increasing major-customer concentration as material risks.

The custom-ASIC model creates a double-edged dependency: deep customer collaboration supports stickiness, while customers can vertically integrate, shift programs, use competing suppliers or change architectures, and third-party IP/manufacturing dependencies can delay ramps.

Record revenue and $605.5M quarterly operating cash flow argue against a present operating-failure thesis; red-team concerns are concentration, supply-chain dependency and expectation/design-win conversion rather than evidence of current collapse.
